I have worked with Brazilian teams for three years. The first difference is time. Meetings in Brazil start more slowly than meetings in the US. In Atlanta, we go to the point faster, and the small talk is shorter. In Sao Paulo, people talk about the weekend first, and the meeting is warmer. Americans are more direct. They speak more directly, even with a client. Brazilians say no more carefully, so I have learned to listen more closely. But my Brazilian colleagues solve problems more creatively than we do, and they react more quickly when a plan changes. Emails are another difference. Brazilian emails are longer and friendlier, and American emails are shorter and more formal. So which culture is better? Neither. The best teams take the best of both.

extra_audio.text: How was the call with the Atlanta team? Fast. They are much more direct than us. Did they say no to the new deadline? Yes, and they said it very directly. Then let's prepare a shorter proposal.
